milestones.claim: Intel reports the release of Tunnel Falls, a 12-qubit silicon spin-qubit research chip.

evidence.quote: Today, Intel announced the release of its newest quantum research chip, Tunnel Falls, a 12-qubit silicon chip

milestones.claim: A Nano Letters paper reports a 12-quantum-dot spin-qubit array, code named Tunnel Falls, in a planar Si/SiGe process, and states the devices enable up to 12 qubits.

evidence.quote: 12-quantum-dot spin-qubit linear arrays, code named Tunnel Falls
enabling up to 12 qubits, which is the largest number of qubits reported in a single device in Si/SiGe
Si quantum wells in a SiGe heterostructure

milestones.claim: A Nature paper reports silicon two-qubit devices designed by Diraq, made in a 300 mm foundry, with single- and two-qubit control fidelities above 99% on all four devices and state-preparation and measurement fidelities up to 99.9%.

evidence.quote: single- and two-qubit control fidelities exceed 99% for all four devices, and the state preparation and measurement fidelities reach up to 99.9%
The qubit devices were designed by Diraq and fabricated at imec in a 300-mm spin-qubit process

milestones.claim: A Nature Communications paper reports coherent control of an eight-dot linear array of silicon spin qubits fabricated in a 300 mm foundry process, with all eight qubits tuned.

evidence.quote: eight-dot linear array of silicon spin qubits fabricated in a 300 mm CMOS-compatible foundry process
All eight qubits are successfully tuned and characterized

milestones.claim: A Nature paper reports an interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs-Al hybrid devices and states that the measurements “do not, by themselves, determine whether the low-energy states detected by interferometry are topological.”

evidence.quote: These measurements do not, by themselves, determine whether the low-energy states detected by interferometry are topological.

evidence.quote: In 2019, our customers began to put application pilots into production.

gaps.why: The Tunnel Falls release says the chip was fabricated in the D1 fabrication facility and does not name the city. newsroom.intel.com returned 403; the Intel IR copy of the release was used.
gaps.would_need: A primary document that names the city or street of the D1 facility that ran this process.

gaps.topic: Intel next-generation chip after Tunnel Falls
gaps.why: The June 2023 release says a next-generation chip based on Tunnel Falls was expected in 2024. No later primary document in this file shows a release or a revised date, so the target is marked missed as an inference from the passed date.
gaps.would_need: A 2024–2026 Intel primary document that either announces the successor chip or withdraws the date.

gaps.why: The release dateline gives Santa Clara only. SEC submissions list 2200 Mission College Blvd, but that JSON was not cited as a filing exhibit.
gaps.would_need: The Intel Form 10-K cover page, which sec.gov refused under the declared user-agent.

gaps.why: The fetched papers describe foundry devices (two-qubit unit cells and an eight-qubit SiMOS array) and do not give a product name. The eight-qubit device is not placed at the UNSW laboratory; the lab opening release does not say this device was measured there.
gaps.would_need: A Diraq document naming a system and the facility where that device was measured.

gaps.topic: Quantum Motion live site and NQCC address
gaps.why: quantummotion.com returned 403. Quotes are from Wayback copies. The September 2025 release says the full-stack computer was deployed at the UK National Quantum Computing Centre and does not name Harwell, Didcot, or a street. No qubit count is stated for that system. No dated qubit roadmap was found.
gaps.would_need: A reachable Quantum Motion or NQCC page that names the testbed address and the system's qubit count, plus a dated roadmap.

gaps.topic: Bloomsbury name in the journal article
gaps.why: The Nature Electronics paper reports 1,024 silicon quantum-dot devices from Quantum Motion and does not use the name Bloomsbury. The system link uses the 2022 press, which names Bloomsbury and 1024 quantum dots. Those dots are not recorded as qubits.
gaps.would_need: A sentence in the paper, or a later primary document, that uses the name Bloomsbury for this device.

gaps.why: The July 2025 roadmap preprint describes device generations and does not give a calendar year for a qubit-count target. Majorana 1 is a company announcement. The Nature paper states that the parity measurements do not, by themselves, determine that the low-energy states are topological. science-style journal HTML was fetched from nature.com for that paper.
gaps.would_need: A Microsoft roadmap document that states a year for a named topological-qubit target.

gaps.why: Fetched pages describe T centres and a spin-photon architecture. They do not name a product processor. The June 2024 result is a preprint (arXiv:2406.01704) hosted as a PDF on photonic.com; no journal version was fetched.
gaps.would_need: A Photonic document naming a system, and a journal version of 2406.01704 if one exists.

gaps.topic: D-Wave Science full text and Germany site
gaps.why: science.org returned 403 for DOI 10.1126/science.ado6285. Peer-review status uses the arXiv journal-reference line (Science 388, 199-204, 2025) and Crossref; the abstract quotes are from the arXiv record. sec.gov/Archives returned 403; the FY2025 10-K was read from a Wayback copy. The 10-K says Advantage2 systems were operational in Canada, the United States, and Germany and names Huntsville, but it does not name the German facility. The product record is therefore not pinned to one site.
gaps.would_need: The Science PDF or HTML, and a primary sentence naming the German installation site.

gaps.why: The 26 February 2026 Form 10-K and the 20 May 2025 release say New York Stock Exchange and NYSE: QBTS. data.sec.gov submissions fetched on 2026-10-02 list the exchange as Nasdaq.
gaps.would_need: A filing or exchange notice after February 2026 if the listing changed.

gaps.why: The FY2025 10-K discusses a gate-model effort, including fluxonium control and the Quantum Circuits acquisition. Those are not annealing systems and are not recorded in this file. No dated annealing qubit-count roadmap beyond the systems already launched was found.
gaps.would_need: A superconducting-modality file for the gate-model program, and an annealing roadmap if D-Wave publishes qubit-count dates.

gaps.topic: Quantum Brilliance sites and qubit counts
gaps.why: The purchase release names QB-QDK2.0 and Fraunhofer IAF without a city. The company page names the Pawsey Supercomputing Centre and Oak Ridge National Laboratory without cities. No qubit count is stated for either machine. Canberra is taken from the dateline, which also lists Stuttgart.
gaps.would_need: A primary sentence with the installation city and the vendor's qubit count.

gaps.why: Optional for this file. A primary page names a 14|15 platform, but it was not fetched and quoted in this pass.
gaps.would_need: A fetched SQC primary document if a later pass adds the donor platform.
